changeTypeExplanation: This change modifies how an existing security capability (identity federation) is implemented but does not introduce new functionality, data types, or system boundaries, so it is categorized as Adaptive rather than Transformative per SCN-CSO-EVA.
changeDescription: Migrate the tenant single sign-on identity provider integration from SAML 2.0 to OIDC, and rotate the associated federation signing certificate.
reason: The current identity provider is deprecating SAML 2.0 support in Q1 2027; migrating to OIDC ahead of that deadline also allows adoption of shorter-lived, more granularly-scoped access tokens.
customerImpact: Tenant administrators will need to reconfigure their identity provider's relying-party settings using new OIDC client credentials, which will be distributed 30 days before cutover along with step-by-step migration guidance. End users will see no change in their login experience.

planAndTimeline.summary: The OIDC integration will be built and validated in a staging environment against a subset of pilot tenants before being rolled out to all tenants in phased waves. **KSI-IAM-ELP** (least privilege) and **KSI-IAM-SNU** (non-user authentication) will be re-validated against the new integration before general availability.

milestones.milestoneDescription: Complete OIDC integration build and internal security review in staging.
Pilot rollout to 3 volunteer tenants with enhanced monitoring.
Independent assessor re-validation of impacted KSIs.
General availability rollout to all remaining tenants.

impactAnalysis: Business and security impact analysis on file at https://trust.meridianfed.com/mocp/evidence/scn-2026-oidc-migration-bia.pdf. Summary: risk of the change is assessed as low given the phased rollout and pre-cutover validation; the primary risk (mis-scoped OIDC token claims) is mitigated by mirroring the current SAML attribute-to-role mapping exactly during the initial rollout.
